Immediate / Intraoperative Complications: Severe Bleeding & Clotting Issues (Excessive blood loss requiring transfusions); Immediate Donor Heart Failure (The new heart fails to pump properly right after implantation); Right Heart Failure (Right side of the heart struggles to pump into the lungs); Irregular Heartbeats (Arrhythmias requiring temporary pacing); Immediate Immune Rejection (Rare, sudden immune reaction against the donor heart); Difficulty Weaning from Bypass (Trouble transitioning off the heart-lung machine); Nerve or Vessel Injury (Temporary strain on nearby nerves controlling voice/diaphragm); Air Bubble in Circulation (Air entering blood vessels during surgery); Suture Line Complications (Slow healing at vascular connection points); Severe Low Blood Pressure (Vasoplegic syndrome requiring blood pressure support)
Early Post-Operative Complications: Early Immune Rejection (Acute reaction detected via routine heart biopsies); Ongoing Heart Pump Support Needed (Temporary mechanical pump support like ECMO); Increased Risk of Infection (Bacterial, viral, or fungal infections due to initial anti-rejection meds); Kidney Stress or Injury (Temporary decrease in kidney function from drugs or pressure changes); Natural Pacemaker Dysfunction (Slow/altered rhythms requiring a pacemaker); Fluid Around the Heart (Pericardial effusion needing drainage); Chest Re-Exploration for Bleeding (Brief surgical return to stop bleeding); Delayed Chest Wound Healing (Slow healing of the sternum incision); Liver Stress (Temporary strain from medications or reduced blood flow); Nervous System Effects (Confusion, seizures, or stroke from medication/pressure changes); High Blood Sugar (Steroid-induced blood sugar spikes); Digestive System Issues (Sluggish bowel movement or GI bleeding)
Late Post-Operative Complications: Narrowing of Heart Arteries (Cardiac Allograft Vasculopathy - CAV); Chronic Rejection & Heart Failure (Gradual weakening of the new heart over time); Increased Risk of Cancers (Post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder or skin cancers from long-term meds); Lifelong Infection Risk (Continued vulnerability to unusual infections); Long-Term Medication Side Effects (Kidney strain, weakened bones, high blood pressure, and cholesterol from anti-rejection meds); Long-Term Kidney Disease (Cumulative drug-induced kidney wear); Silent Heart Warning Signs (Denervation masking typical chest pain during heart strain); Emotional & Mental Health Strain (Anxiety or depression surrounding chronic care)
